CLIPORA / GUIDE

Paste the words. Leave the formatting.

A copied paragraph can bring along a font, background color or link style. Plain-text paste keeps its text while leaving the source styling behind.

Reviewed 29 October 2026 · Clipora editorial

On this page
First, try the destination’s plain-paste commandUse Clipora’s plain-paste actionConvert a one-off paragraph in your browserFormatting and line breaks are different

First, try the destination’s plain-paste command

Many browsers and editors use Ctrl + Shift + V. It is not a universal Windows shortcut: some applications use it for a different action. Look for Paste as plain text, Keep Text Only or Paste Special in the destination’s menu.

A simple alternative is to paste into a plain-text editor, copy the text there and paste that into your destination. Review line breaks and tabs before using the result.

Source: Microsoft’s Windows keyboard shortcut reference.

Use Clipora’s plain-paste action

  1. Copy the formatted paragraph while Clipora is running.
  2. Click your destination and open quick access with Ctrl + Alt + V.
  3. Select the saved text and use Alt + Enter, or choose the plain-text paste action in its menu.

If the destination blocks automated input, use copy and the destination’s paste command. Plain text removes rich formatting; it does not rewrite the words or strip every line break.

Convert a one-off paragraph in your browser

The plain-text tool accepts a normal paste, shows the text-only result and lets you copy it deliberately. Processing stays in this tab. It does not read your clipboard in the background, save the input or send the text to a server.

HTML source pasted as characters stays literal text. The tool never renders it as a page or executes a script.

Formatting and line breaks are different

Removing styling keeps the copied text’s newlines. Text copied from a PDF can therefore still be broken into short lines. Use the line-break remover to join those lines, with an option to preserve paragraph breaks.

Plain-text conversion may lose rich-text details such as a link’s hidden destination or table structure. Keep the original until you have checked the result.
